Si le donneur a gagné, ou s’il était ten: If the dealer won, or was tenpai at the draw, they keep the deal (renchan) and place a counter, the honba: each honba adds 300 points to the next win. Otherwise, the deal passes to the player on the right and the winds rotate.
Sur internet et dans les livres, on écri: Online and in books, hands are written in shorthand: the numbers, then a letter for the suit. m for characters (man), p for circles (pin), s for bamboo (sou), z for honours, numbered 1 to 7 (East, South, West, North, white, green, red). A 0 is the red five.

Un 5 rouge par famille, chacun vaut un d: One red 5 per suit, each worth one dora.
Un brelan : trois tuiles identiques. Ouv: A triplet: three identical tiles. Open if it was called (pon), concealed otherwise.
Un brelan de dragons, du vent de la manc: A triplet of dragons, of the round wind or of your seat wind: a one-han yaku, allowed in an open hand.
Un brelan fermé, formé sans appel. Il ra: A concealed triplet, made without a call. It is worth twice as many fu as an open triplet.
Un carré : quatre tuiles identiques. On: A quad: four identical tiles. You then draw a replacement tile and a new dora indicator is turned over.
Un cinq rouge. Chacun vaut un dora : un: A red five. Each one is worth a dora: one more han if the hand wins. Sets usually have three, one per suit.
Un groupe de trois ou quatre tuiles : su: A set of three or four tiles: run, triplet or quad. You need four of them to win.
Un jeu de riichi compte 136 tuiles : 34: A riichi set has 136 tiles: 34 different kinds, four copies of each. They fall into two groups: numbered tiles, split into three suits from 1 to 9, and honours, which have no number.
Un jour manqué se rattrape : touchez sa: Missed a day? Catch up: tap its square.

Un non-donneur gagne sur sa première pio: A non-dealer wins on their first draw, with no calls before.
Un yaku d’un han : gagner dans le tour q: A one-han yaku: winning within one turn of your riichi declaration, before any call.
Un yaku d’un han : main fermée de quatre: A one-han yaku: a closed hand of four runs, a valueless pair and a ryanmen wait. The hand only counts the base fu: 20 on tsumo, 30 on ron.
Un yaku est une combinaison reconnue : s: A yaku is a recognised combination: no yaku, no win, even with four sets and a pair. There are about forty, but these cover most of a beginner’s hands:
Une combinaison qui rapporte des han. Il: A combination that brings han. You need at least one yaku to win: dora alone are not enough.
Une de chaque terminale et de chaque hon: One of each terminal and honour, plus a second copy of one of them.
Une donne nulle, le plus souvent parce q: A drawn hand, most often because the wall runs out with no winner. Noten players pay tenpai players.
Une donne s’arrête quand un joueur gagne: A hand ends when a player wins, or when the wall runs out with no winner: it is a drawn hand (ryuukyoku). Tenpai players then show their hands, and noten players pay them 3,000 points in total.
Une fois qu’on a un yaku, chaque dora aj: Once you have a yaku, each dora adds one han: the tile after the indicator, each red five, and with riichi, the ura-dora. A hand can go from 1 to 4 han thanks to its dora.

Une main de riichi à compter :steps. Le: A riichi hand to score :steps. The link always brings back the same hand.
Une main déjà gagnée, à compter en cinq: A hand already won, to score in five steps, checked and explained.
Une main en attente d’une seule tuile: A hand waiting on a single tile
Une main en riichi qui gagne retourne au: A riichi hand that wins also turns over the tiles hidden under the indicators: these are the ura-dora, read the same way.
Une main est tenpai quand il ne lui manq: A hand is tenpai when it only needs one more tile to win. The tiles that complete it are its waits.
Une main fermée, sans aucun appel (un ka: A closed hand, with no calls at all (a concealed kan is allowed). Riichi, pinfu and menzen tsumo require it.
Une main ouverte à 20 fu est portée à 30: An open hand at 20 fu is raised to 30 fu.
Une main refaite sans faute quitte la li: A hand replayed without mistakes leaves the list.
Une paire de vent à la fois du siège et: A pair of a wind that is both seat and round wind: 4 fu instead of 2.
Une partie de riichi enchaîne des donnes: A game of riichi is a series of short hands: everyone draws and discards in turn, until a player completes their hand. Here is everything that happens at the table, in order.
Une règle optionnelle qui arrondit au ma: An optional rule that rounds up hands of 4 han 30 fu and 3 han 60 fu, which pay almost as much, to a mangan.
Une suite : trois tuiles qui se suivent: A run: three consecutive tiles in the same suit, like 3-4-5 of circles. Honours can’t form one.
Une technique de défense : si un joueur: A defence technique: if a player has discarded the 4, they can’t win on the 1 or the 7 with a ryanmen wait.
Une tuile bonus, désignée par l’indicate: A bonus tile, shown by the indicator turned over on the dead wall. Each dora in the winning hand adds one han, but it is not a yaku.
Une tuile déjà défaussée par un adversai: A tile an opponent has already discarded: it cannot win them the hand (furiten). It is the safest discard against a riichi.
Une tuile qui vient d’être défaussée peu: A tile that has just been discarded can be taken by another player to complete a set. You call it out loud, then lay the set face up to the right of your hand.
Uniquement des tuiles de 2 à 8, aucun ho: Only tiles from 2 to 8, no honours or terminals.
Victoire avant votre prochaine défausse: Win before your next discard after riichi, with no call in between.
Victoire sur la tuile piochée après un k: Win on the tile drawn after a kan.
Victoire sur votre propre pioche avec un: Win on your own draw with a closed hand (closed kans don’t open it).

Être furiten, c’est avoir l’une de ses t: Being furiten means having one of your winning tiles in your own discards. You can then no longer win by ron, only by tsumo.
